## Load packages

A few R symbols recur throughout the site: `<-` stores a result under a name; `%>%` passes the result on the left into the next operation; `$` selects a named column; and `[["name"]]` selects an item from a named list. Read a pipeline from top to bottom, asking how each step changes the rows or columns.

A package supplies functions that R does not provide on its own. `library()` attaches an already installed package for this session; it does not install it. Here, readxl reads spreadsheets, dplyr/tidyr (within tidyverse) reshape data, MASS and lme4 fit models, and the table and plotting packages format the output. If R reports that a package is missing, the setup has not finished.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| eval: false
```

## Data paths

`COHERO_DATA_DIR` is a setting supplied by an authorized analyst outside the repository. `Sys.getenv()` reads that setting and `file.path()` combines it with each filename. The explicit `stop()` prevents the script from continuing with an unspecified data folder. Reading this website does not require the files: its code blocks are displayed, not executed.

```{r}
#| label: data-paths
#| eval: false
```

## Define constants

These named objects collect the visit cutoff, questionnaire item lists, medication names, outcomes and subgroup variables used later. A vector such as `count_outcomes` is a list of column names; later loops repeat the same operation for each name. Changing a threshold or item list changes the analysis definition, so its justification belongs in the [analysis plan](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/blob/main/analysis-plan.md), not just in this file.

```{r}
#| label: define-constants
#| eval: false
```

## Figure labels

`figure_labels` gives each variable a readable name for figures, so a reader sees "ACT score" rather than `act_score`. `arm_labels` names the arms in place of their codes, 0 and 1. The figure style on [Plot style](plot_style.qmd) uses both. The labels give names and units only: each instrument's range and direction will be added once its scoring source is confirmed in the analysis plan.

```{r}
#| label: figure-labels
#| eval: false
```

## Output folders

Tables are saved to `tables/` in the project and figures, once they are exported, to `figures/`; these lines name the two folders and create them if needed. Setting `COHERO_OUTPUT_DIR` (for example in `.Renviron`, like `COHERO_DATA_DIR`) sends both to another folder instead. The synthetic-data runs in `tests/synthetic/` set it to a temporary folder, so a test run can never overwrite tables made from the study data. [Tables](tables.qmd#export-tables) saves every table as a Word file; the figure script keeps its plots in memory. For help with scripts, projects and finding function help, see the corresponding chapters of [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) [@r4ds2].

```{r}

#| eval: false
```
